metadata.case_name: YEUNG KIU YING v. FAIRWOOD FAST FOOD LTD T/A FAIRWOOD

plaintiff.education_level: educated in the PRC up to secondary school F4 level and can read and write simple Chinese

injuries.description: right trigger thumb / right thumb sprain (aggravated by the Accident) with residual symptoms
source: the plaintiff had been suffering from right trigger thumb prior to the Accident.
History of injury at work: yes, right thumb sprain when a stack of plates fell onto her…
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of thumb, unspecified

manifestations.description: diffuse tenderness of the whole right thumb
sensation much reduced over whole right thumb
complete loss of right hand grip strength
active 45° of right thumb, passive 60° of right thumb (reduced active range of motion)
mild residual pain and stiffness over the right thumb and mild tenderness over the MCP joint

treatments_received.treatment: consultation at a private medical practitioner near her home on 18 October 2012
source: the plaintiff says she went to a private medical practitioner near her home on 18 October 2012, the day of the Alleged Accident.

treatments_received.treatment: attendance at Kwong Wah Hospital A&E on 19 October 2012
source: The plaintiff attended the A&E department of Kwong Wah Hospital the day after the Accident on 19 October 2012.
the plaintiff had received a right thumb injection in July 2012.

treatments_received.treatment: injection and referral to orthopaedics specialist clinic and occupational therapy (22 October 2012)
source: She was given an injection and was referred to the orthopaedics specialist clinic and occupational therapy.

treatments_received.treatment: right thumb operation to release her right trigger finger on 2 November 2012
source: on 2 November 2012 she received right thumb operation there.
On 2 November 2012 she received right thumb operation to release her right trigger finger.

losses.description: mild residual pain and stiffness over the right thumb and mild tenderness over the MCP joint

comparable_cases.case_name: Ting Siu Ki v Wun Che Ming & Anor
